skiResorts.scoreHelp: A reference score: weather 60% (rain, strong wind, cold and warmth lower it; fresh snow raises it) and weekday/holiday crowds 40%. Winter break (late Dec–Feb) can be busy even on weekdays.

tips.title: Avoiding crowds
items: Weekends, holidays and winter break (late Dec–Feb) mean long lift lines. Weekday mornings are best.
Only some slopes open early in the season; check the official site for today’s slopes.
Lift tickets, season passes and shuttle buses differ by resort; check before you go.

weather.title: Reading the weather
items: Rain hurts snow the most; above freezing, precipitation can fall as rain.
Fresh snow is welcome, but heavy snow blocks roads. Bring chains or winter tires.
The summit is colder and windier than the base; this forecast is for near the base.

season.title: Season timing
items: High Gangwon resorts usually open first in late November, the Seoul area in early December and the south in mid-December.
Seasons usually end in early to mid March; Phoenix plans to run until March 14, 2027.
Opening dates change with weather and snowmaking, so check again before leaving.

items.q: When do Korean ski resorts open in 2026?
items.a: As of Nov 22, Mona Yongpyong and Phoenix Snow Park opened first on Nov 22. High1 targets Nov 24, Muju Deogyusan Nov 27, Alpensia Nov 28, Elysian Gangchon Dec 4 and Oak Valley Dec 11. Vivaldi Park, Welli Hilli, Konjiam, Jisan and Eden Valley have not announced a date yet.
High, cold Pyeongchang resorts such as Mona Yongpyong and Phoenix usually open first. This year both opened on the same day, Nov 22.

items.q: How do I pick a good day?
items.a: A dry, calm weekday is best. Rain spoils the snow and strong wind can stop lifts. This page scores each forecast day by weather and weekday.

items.q: Which resorts are closest to Seoul?
items.a: Konjiam (Gwangju, Gyeonggi) and Jisan (Icheon) are about an hour from Seoul; Elysian Gangchon, Vivaldi Park and Oak Valley are also close.
